questions.q: ECI's ASDD directive (6 Nov 2026) lets affected SIR voters resubmit which document instead of Form 6?
questions.explanation: ASDD (Absent/Shifted/Dead/Duplicate) voters can resubmit the enumeration form with a statement, rather than Form 6, which is meant for first-time registration.
questions.fact_text: ECI directed that voters marked **ASDD (Absent/Shifted/Dead/Duplicate)** in **7** States/UTs under SIR (Delhi, Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana, Nagaland) can resubmit their **enumeration form** (not Form 6) to get re-included in the rolls; follows a SC query during the Oct 28 Bhardwaj-Johri hearing.

questions.q: In the Mustafabad Form-7 case, how many of the 37 scrutinised deletion applications were found 'fabricated'?
questions.explanation: The DEO's office found 36 of 37 Form-7 applications fabricated (only 1 was genuine); Section 31 of the RP Act was invoked.
questions.fact_text: Mustafabad (Delhi) Form-7 case: the ERO sought an FIR against BJP booth-level agent Chandra Shekhar Nainwal; DEO scrutiny found **36 of 37** Form-7 deletion applications "fabricated" (only 1 true); **Section 31 of the RP Act** invoked for false declaration.

questions.q: The editorial says using voter-roll data to verify welfare beneficiaries contradicts the SC's judgment on which State's SIR?
questions.explanation: The SC's May 27 judgment on the Bihar SIR held that ECI's citizenship enquiry is 'limited' and its consequence confined to the electoral roll alone.
questions.fact_text: Editorial: Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh's plan to use voter ID + biometrics to verify welfare beneficiaries (Rahul Gandhi called it "rights theft") contradicts the **SC's May 27 judgment** on Bihar SIR, which held ECI's citizenship enquiry is "limited" and its consequence confined to electoral rolls alone, not welfare eligibility.

questions.q: The Gauhati HC quashed the NSA detention of activist Pranab Doley, who had protested against a project near which national park?
questions.explanation: Doley protested a luxury hotel project near Kaziranga National Park and was freed after 118 days in custody.
questions.fact_text: Gauhati HC quashed the **NSA detention** of Assam land-rights activist Pranab Doley (Greater Kaziranga Land and Human Rights Protection Committee), held since July over protests against a luxury hotel near Kaziranga National Park; released after **118 days** in custody.

questions.q: Per the SC-cited I4C data, digital-arrest complaints on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal fell to how many in H1 2026?
questions.explanation: Complaints fell from 1,23,672 (2024) to 58,249 (2025) to 16,377 for the period ending June 30, 2026.
questions.fact_text: SC (CJI Surya Kant) said **cybercriminals** "have no space in society" and jails "are only meant for them" while rejecting a bail plea; cited I4C data showing digital-arrest complaints fell from **1,23,672** (2024) to **58,249** (2025) to **16,377** (H1 2026); e-Zero FIR mechanism functional in **19** States.

questions.q: The SC declined to suspend Tarun Tejpal's sentence in a rape case from which State?
questions.explanation: The case is the 2013 Goa rape case; the Bombay HC's Goa Bench had overturned his trial-court acquittal in August.
questions.fact_text: SC declined to suspend journalist **Tarun Tejpal**'s 10-year sentence in the 2013 Goa rape case (Bombay HC's August verdict overturning his trial-court acquittal), but agreed to hear his appeal.

questions.q: The ED's plea against a quashed NewsClick money-laundering case alleged FDI violations of about how much?
questions.explanation: The EOW's 2020 FIR alleged NewsClick's parent company received ₹9.59 crore in FDI from a US entity in violation of foreign-investment law.
questions.fact_text: SC sought responses from news portal **NewsClick** and editor Prabir Purkayastha on an ED plea against a Delhi HC order quashing a money-laundering case over alleged **₹9.59 crore** FDI-rule violations (from Worldwide Media Holdings LLC, US, in FY 2018-19).

questions.q: The SC's contempt notice to KPCC office-bearers concerned a social-media post targeting whom?
questions.explanation: The post against CJI Surya Kant prompted the SC to say judicial independence 'is not a matter of political convenience.'
questions.fact_text: SC issued notice to Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee office-bearers on a contempt plea over a (now-deleted) social-media post against CJI Surya Kant, saying "the independence of the judiciary is not a matter of political convenience."

questions.q: The Jharkhand HC quashed the State's cancellation of which recruitment exam?
questions.explanation: The HC quashed the cancellation of the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission Combined Graduate Level (JSSC-CGL) exam and ordered reinstatement of selected candidates.
questions.fact_text: Jharkhand HC quashed the State's cancellation of the **JSSC-CGL** recruitment exam and ordered reinstatement, with continuous service, of candidates selected under advertisement 10/2023; held the government gave no concrete evidence of systemic irregularities.

questions.q: NC chief Farooq Abdullah met how many dissident MLAs before ruling out a party split?
questions.explanation: Farooq Abdullah met 17 disgruntled legislators and assured a step-by-step approach to their demands.
questions.fact_text: NC chief Farooq Abdullah ruled out a party split after meeting **17** dissident MLAs; Speaker Om Birla accepted Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi's resignation from the party and his Lok Sabha seat, effective November 3.

questions.q: Amit Shah set a BJP target of winning how many of Uttarakhand's 70 Assembly seats?
questions.explanation: Shah called for a 'hat-trick' in Uttarakhand, targeting more than 65 of the State's 70 seats.
questions.fact_text: Union Home Minister Amit Shah set a "hat-trick" target of over **65** of Uttarakhand's **70** Assembly seats for the BJP at the State's 26th Foundation Day event.

questions.q: The SC clarified that its March 11, 2026 OBC creamy-layer judgment does NOT require what?
options: Retrospective revision of past service allocations/seniority
questions.explanation: Justice Mahadevan held the judgment determines only the rights of parties who approached the court, not a general revision of past allocations or seniority.
questions.fact_text: SC clarified its **March 11, 2026** OBC non-creamy-layer judgment (excluding parental salary/agri income from the income test) does **not** require retrospective revision of service allocations or seniority across recruitment years; Civil Services Exam 2025 results (declared March 6) stand, with the creamy-layer principle only governing fresh allocation.

questions.q: CBSE's 2027 Class 10 and 12 board exams will begin on which date?
questions.explanation: The 2027 boards begin February 16; Class 10 concludes March 9 and Class 12 concludes April 9.
questions.fact_text: CBSE's 2027 Class 10 and 12 board exams will begin **February 16** (Class 10 ends March 9, Class 12 ends April 9); Class 10 has 83 subjects and Class 12 has 121 subjects on offer; **26.5 lakh** Class 10 and **19.8 lakh** Class 12 students have registered.

questions.q: Centre's weekly rice/paddy stock-declaration mandate for traders invokes which law?
questions.explanation: Non-compliant units face action under Sections 6 and 7 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955.
questions.fact_text: Centre mandated weekly rice/paddy stock declaration (6 categories) by traders on the Food Stock Portal under **Sections 6 and 7 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955**; let 5 southern States (AP, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Telangana) impose stock limits till Jan 31, 2027; doubled the OMSS e-auction target for 2026-27 from 25 to **50 lakh tonnes**.

questions.q: The SC called Delhi's vehicle and construction bans for pollution control:
questions.explanation: The SC asked if the government had any scientific method beyond these 'old, tried and failed tools', as Delhi's AQI crossed 400.
questions.fact_text: SC termed Delhi's vehicle/construction bans "old, tried and **failed tools**" for pollution control and asked if the Centre/CAQM had any scientific alternative; Delhi's AQI crossed **400** (GRAP-III) hours after the hearing; CJI Surya Kant said curbing pollution needs public behaviour change, not just court orders.

questions.q: The Siang Upper Multipurpose Project's push is partly justified by countering China's dam on which river?
questions.explanation: China's Medog dam on the Yarlung-Tsangpo (which feeds the Brahmaputra via the Siang) is cited as a reason to speed up India's SUMP.
questions.fact_text: Ground report on the **Siang Upper Multipurpose Project** (11,000 MW, declared a national project in 2008): Adi community opposition via the Siang Indigenous Farmers' Forum; China's under-construction **Medog dam** on the Yarlung-Tsangpo (which feeds the Brahmaputra) is cited to justify speeding up the project; Article 371(h) of the Constitution (special provisions for Arunachal/Nagaland) referenced.

questions.q: The SC's settlement of the 1966 Bhakra-Beas power dispute gives Himachal Pradesh how many million units of electricity over 20 years?
questions.explanation: Himachal Pradesh will get 11,973 million units from Punjab and Haryana, per the shares fixed by the 2011 SC verdict (HP 7.19%).
questions.fact_text: SC settled a **1966** Bhakra-Beas energy dues dispute: Himachal Pradesh will get **11,973 million units** of power from Punjab and Haryana over 20 years (per the 2011 SC verdict fixing shares at HP 7.19%, Punjab 51.80%, Haryana 37.51%, Chandigarh 3.50%), with no cash payment required.

questions.q: On 6 November 2026, the Nifty50 closed at its highest level since which date?
questions.explanation: The Nifty closed at 25,030.35, its highest since March 2, in its biggest weekly rally of 2026 (+6.8%).
questions.fact_text: Sensex rose 2.17% (1,718 pts) to **81,028.02** and Nifty 2.01% to **25,030.35** (highest since March 2) on Nov 6 — the Nifty's biggest weekly rally of 2026 (+6.8%) — even as the Nasdaq-100 fell **6.36%** on Nov 5 (wiping ~$2.53 trillion), on AI-infrastructure-spending fears after the US midterms; the rupee hit a 6-month high of **93.89**/$.

questions.q: Mumbai NCLT declared which Videocon-linked individual 'bankrupt' over a ₹12,668 crore default to SBI?
questions.explanation: Venugopal Nandlal Dhoot, former Videocon promoter, was declared bankrupt by the Mumbai NCLT bench.
questions.fact_text: Mumbai NCLT declared Videocon Industries' former promoter **Venugopal Dhoot** "bankrupt" over a **₹12,668 crore** default to SBI, admitting the lender's petition and appointing a bankruptcy trustee.

questions.q: NPCI's new tech subsidiary, set up to focus on AI, blockchain and GCC services, is called:
questions.explanation: NTSL will focus on AI, blockchain, GCC services and support DPI programmes; Vishal Kanvaty is its MD & CEO.
questions.fact_text: NPCI set up a wholly owned subsidiary, **NPCI Tech Solutions Ltd (NTSL)**, to focus on AI, blockchain and GCC services beyond its core payments mandate; Vishal Kanvaty named MD & CEO.

questions.q: The government's latest ECMS approvals take total committed investment in electronics component manufacturing to about:
questions.explanation: ₹77,051 crore across 118 approved projects, about 30% above the original ₹59,350-crore target.
questions.fact_text: Govt approved 12 more projects under the **Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS)**, taking total approvals to 118 and committed investment to **₹77,051 crore** (~30% above the original ₹59,350-crore target); the biggest is a ₹3,546-crore copper-foil facility by Indo Asia Copper Ltd in Amreli, Gujarat.

questions.q: Delhi Police booked the Chawri Bazar collapse's contractors under which section for culpable homicide not amounting to murder?
questions.explanation: The contractors (Siraj, Tajuddin, Furkan) were booked under Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
questions.fact_text: Delhi Police arrested 3 contractors (Siraj, Tajuddin, Furkan) over the Chawri Bazar building collapse, booked under **BNS Section 105** (culpable homicide not amounting to murder); 4 workers remained missing on the second day of rescue operations.

questions.q: The Ken-Betwa river-linking project's dam near Daudhan village is on which river, and roughly how many trees will it require felling?
questions.explanation: The 96.7-metre dam on the Ken will require felling an estimated 2.3 million trees, affecting about 8,000 Adivasi families across 22 villages.
questions.fact_text: Op-ed on Panna/Chhatarpur (M.P.) displacement by the Majhgaya dam, Runjh dam and **Ken-Betwa river-linking project** (a 96.7-metre dam near Daudhan on the Ken): about **8,000 Adivasi families** across 22 villages affected; **2.3 million trees** to be felled; FRA Section 4(5) rights-recognition not completed before eviction; activist Divya Ahirwar, jailed since Sept 27 on a fabricated charge, granted HC bail.

questions.q: Congress's renewed demand to scrap Agnipath came a day after what Cabinet decision?
options: A 2-year extension for Agniveers after their 4-year tenure
questions.explanation: The Union Cabinet had approved a two-year extension for Agniveers completing their initial four-year tenure, with possible permanent recruitment thereafter.
questions.fact_text: Congress renewed its demand to scrap Agnipath, alleging a shortfall of over **2 lakh** soldiers and that **1.5 lakh** recruited candidates' joining was halted; alleged over **40** Agniveer suicides — a day after the Cabinet's 2-year-extension clarification.

also.text: The government clarified **Agnipath is not rolled back**: the 25% retained after 4 years continue as before, while the remaining 75% get a second 2-year engagement, after which all willing and fit Agniveers can join the regular cadre with **protected seniority**.

questions.q: The Kochon Prize 2026, won by Chennai-based REACH, recognises contributions to fighting which disease?
questions.explanation: REACH is the first Indian civil-society organisation to win the Kochon Prize, awarded for contributions to the fight against TB.
questions.fact_text: Chennai-based TB nonprofit **REACH** won the **Kochon Prize 2026**, the first Indian civil-society organisation to do so; shared with Kenya's Centre for Health Solutions and the Marshall Islands TB Control Program.

questions.q: Brent crude fell 16% this week after Iran opened the Strait of Hormuz for transit to a few countries including:
questions.explanation: Iran opened the Strait of Hormuz for transit to a few countries including India, reviving hopes of a US-Iran war resolution.
questions.fact_text: Brent crude fell **16%** this week (steepest since the pandemic) after Iran opened the Strait of Hormuz for transit to a few countries, including India, reviving hopes of a US-Iran war resolution; Iran's Revolutionary Guards separately said two more tankers caught fire in the Strait.

questions.q: India-born Nithya Raman was elected Mayor of which US city, defeating incumbent Karen Bass?
questions.explanation: Raman, a Democratic Socialist, won with 52% of the vote against Bass's 48% in the Los Angeles mayoral race.
questions.fact_text: India-born Democratic Socialist **Nithya Raman** was elected Mayor of Los Angeles, defeating incumbent Karen Bass **52%-48%**.

questions.q: In Israel, who does Gadi Eisenkot expect to give him the government-formation mandate?
questions.explanation: Eisenkot expects President Isaac Herzog to hand him the mandate to form a government on Sunday.
questions.fact_text: Israel: Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot said he expects President Isaac Herzog to give him the government-formation mandate on Sunday; Opposition partner Avigdor Liberman lifted his veto on ultra-Orthodox military-service demands but still refuses an alliance with Israeli-Arab parties.

questions.q: The 13th ICAPP General Assembly, held in Seoul, adopted which declaration on non-interference and peaceful dispute settlement?
questions.explanation: 83 political parties from across Asia unanimously adopted the Seoul Declaration at ICAPP's 13th General Assembly.
questions.fact_text: The **13th ICAPP General Assembly** (Seoul, Nov 4-6; 83 Asian political parties) adopted the "Seoul Declaration", stressing non-interference, peaceful dispute settlement and adherence to the UN Charter amid rising unilateral actions.

questions.q: The US recorded how many confirmed measles cases this year, the highest since 1991?
questions.explanation: 5,182 confirmed cases were recorded this year, despite measles being declared eliminated in the US in 2000.
questions.fact_text: The US recorded **5,182** confirmed measles cases this year, the highest since 1991; measles was declared eliminated in the US in 2000.

questions.q: Indian GM V. Pranav won the Open title at the FIDE World Junior Blitz Championship, held in:
questions.explanation: Pranav (20, Chennai) won with 10.5/13 points in Al Ain, adding to his existing World Junior Classical title.
questions.fact_text: Indian GM **V. Pranav** (20, Chennai) won the Open title at the FIDE World Junior Blitz Championship in Al Ain (10.5/13 points), having already won the World Junior Classical title; he also took rapid silver at the same event.

questions.q: Mohammed Shami retired from Test cricket with 229 wickets from how many matches?
questions.explanation: Shami played 64 Tests over a 13-year career, debuting against West Indies at Eden Gardens on this date in 2013.
questions.fact_text: Mohammed Shami retired from Test cricket with **229 wickets in 64 matches** over a 13-year career (debut vs West Indies, Eden Gardens, Nov 6, 2013); best figures 5/28 (Johannesburg, 2018); last Test was the 2023 WTC final at the Oval.

questions.q: Mitchell Starc's 460 Test wickets make him the most successful bowler of which type in Test history?
questions.explanation: Starc reached 460 wickets in 110 Tests, the most by any left-arm pacer ever, passing Wasim Akram's 414 in the 2025-26 Ashes.
questions.fact_text: Mitchell Starc reached **460 wickets in 110 Tests** (avg 25.97) — the most by any left-arm pacer in history — having passed Wasim Akram's 414 during the 2025-26 Ashes; his 2025 calendar year yielded 55 wickets in 11 Tests at an average of 17.32.

questions.q: Dhinidhi Desinghu won India's first-ever Youth Olympics aquatics medals (bronze) in which two events?
questions.explanation: She won bronze in both 100m freestyle (a new Indian women's best of 56.27s) and 200m freestyle (2:02.28s) at the Dakar Youth Olympics.
questions.fact_text: India won its first-ever **aquatics medals at the Youth Olympics** (Dakar 2026, the 4th edition since 2010): Dhinidhi Desinghu won bronze in both 100m freestyle (56.27s, a new Indian women's best) and 200m freestyle (2:02.28s); Tirthank Pegu won bronze in men's 200m butterfly (2:01.25s), India's first male swimming medal at the Games.

also.text: Tanvi Patri won badminton silver at the Dakar Youth Olympics, losing the final to World junior champion Zhang Yi Xin of China 21-15, 13-21, 24-26.

questions.q: Tanvi Patri's badminton final loss at the Dakar Youth Olympics was to which player?
questions.explanation: Patri won silver after losing 21-15, 13-21, 24-26 to World junior champion Zhang Yi Xin of China.
questions.fact_text: Tanvi Patri won badminton silver at the Dakar Youth Olympics, losing the final to World junior champion Zhang Yi Xin of China 21-15, 13-21, 24-26.
